name: Amanda Gonzalez

summary.text: Amanda Gonzalez is the elected Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder, an attorney, and an adjunct law professor at the University of Denver.
She is a former executive director of Colorado Common Cause.
She earned a bachelor's degree from Occidental College in 2006 and a law degree from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law in 2011.

experience.text: Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder, elected 2022.
Former Executive Director of Colorado Common Cause; taught election law at the University of Denver.
Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary for Secretary of State with 64.4% of the vote over Jessie Danielson.

record.title: Response to federal voter-list demand
record.detail: As Jefferson County Clerk, said Colorado had already refused to give the Trump administration its voter data in response to a U.S. Postal Service proposal conditioning mail-ballot delivery on states sharing voter lists.

record.title: Opposed shortening Tina Peters' sentence
record.detail: Said she disagreed with Gov. Jared Polis' decision to shorten former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters' prison sentence, saying it 'sends the wrong message to voters and the wrong message to election workers.'

record.title: Voter roll purge attempt
record.detail: Campaign states she blocked an attempt to remove 23,000 voters from Jefferson County's rolls using legal loopholes; this record is self-reported by her campaign and not independently verified by a news outlet in this research session.

record.title: Election administration record in Jefferson County
record.detail: Campaign states Jefferson County delivered the most ballots cast of any Colorado county in two election cycles under her tenure, came in under budget, and received EAC Clearinghouse election-innovation awards in 2023, 2024 and 2025; self-reported by her campaign.

record.title: Supported 2024 jail voting-access law
record.detail: As Jefferson County Clerk, cited her work on a 2024 Colorado law requiring access to in-person voting at all county jails as part of her record on expanding voting access; exact date within 2024 not given by this source.

positions.source_title: Where James Wiley and Amanda Gonzalez stand on the top issues in the Colorado secretary of state's race
positions.quote: Every ballot that we count is a paper ballot and you can't hack paper.
positions.note: Answering 'Yes' to The Colorado Sun's question of whether she supports continuing Colorado's practice of automatically mailing ballots to registered voters and counting them with machines.

positions.source_title: Where James Wiley and Amanda Gonzalez stand on the top issues in the Colorado secretary of state's race
positions.quote: I am interested in solving actual problems in our elections and finding ways to make it more accessible for voters, not creating new hoops for eligible voters to jump through.
positions.note: Directly asked whether she supports Amendment 84. She said she does not take official positions on ballot measures, but these are her own words answering that question, so this is coded as a qualified disagree rather than inferred.

positions.source_title: Where James Wiley and Amanda Gonzalez stand on the top issues in the Colorado secretary of state's race
positions.quote: It is clearly not the president's role to regulate how Colorado runs our elections. He should particularly not be doing that for partisan purposes.
positions.note: Answering how Colorado should respond to possible federal attempts to limit mail voting, she said it is not the president's role to regulate the state's elections; support for challenging such actions is inferred from that.

research_notes: The Colorado Sun's Oct. 7, 2026 candidate guide directly asked Gonzalez about Amendment 84 and confirmed she declines to take official positions on ballot measures; mail-ballot-id is coded from her own words in that answer rather than from party or general inference. No statement found naming Amendment 85 or 86 specifically, so plain-language-ballots and redistricting-commission are left unsourced (unknown). Two 'decision' record items sourced to her own campaign site (voter-roll purge defense, Jeffco election-administration record) are self-reported and not independently verified against a news outlet in this session -- a reviewer should check these before publishing. Second pass 2026-10-14: checked the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 SoS candidate Q&A and Robert Tann's Oct. 4, 2026 Denver Post article on the race; added one record item (the 2024 jail voting-access law) from the latter. Both sources reinforce her existing keep-mail-voting and challenge-federal-policies positions and do not address plain-language-ballots or redistricting-commission, so no new positions were added.
